title: Setup: show what people can really do and what really changed, using names rather than ids
body:
epic:#26676#1 · zhuangjianguo · session_cdb7a717def74e719988f089fbaa18ff

From a real-user walkthrough of Setup, filed on the maintainer's word: 「以上都同意，立卡」 (2026-11-05). Measured on `main` `b7075d9908`, with the console in dev mode, unless a line says otherwise. Test app scaffolded with `create-objectstack@18.3.0`.

An administrator investigating a problem cannot get an answer from these screens today.

## Items

| # | Where | Observed | Suggestion |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | User record, 权限集 tab | Shows 0 and 暂无相关记录 for a user who has access through the default sets and positions | Show effective access and where it comes from. `POST /api/v1/security/explain` already answers this |
| 2 | Sharing rule record | 接收方 shows a raw id, `_sGHMyWlqcx6t…`; 条件 shows `{"priority":"urgent"}` | The recipient's name, and the condition in words |
| 3 | 审计日志 list | The 记录 column is an id; object names like `Platform Setting Audit Entry` are English; one sign-in writes several rows | Record label; localized names; a default view that hides the machinery |
| 4 | 审计日志 config change detail | Shows the key and a `sha256:` digest, so the new value cannot be read | Show old and new values for non-secret settings. Secrets stay withheld |
| 5 | 共享规则 new form | The object picker lists 86 objects, mostly `sys_*`, with business objects buried | Business objects first; hide objects where a rule makes no sense |
| 6 | Queue record | No way to see or add members from the queue; they are on a separate nav entry | A members list on the queue |

Row 5 includes objects holding credentials and sessions, so the dev should confirm what a rule on those would do while deciding what to hide.
